+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from _pytest._io.wcwidth import wcswidth
+
+
+def unicode_trimmed(format: str, msg: str, available_width: int) -> str | None:
+    """Format msg into format, ellipsizing it if doesn't fit in available_width.
+
+    Like ``_format_trimmed`` in ``_pytest.terminal``, but uses a single Unicode
+    ellipsis character (``…``) instead of three periods, for compact output.
+
+    Returns None if even the ellipsis can't fit.
+    """
+    # Only use the first line.
+    i = msg.find("\n")
+    if i != -1:
+        msg = msg[:i]
+
+    ellipsis = "\N{HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS}"
+    ellipsis_width = wcswidth(ellipsis)
+    format_width = wcswidth(format.format(""))
+    if format_width + ellipsis_width > available_width:
+        return None
+
+    if format_width + wcswidth(msg) > available_width:
+        available_width -= ellipsis_width
+        msg = msg[:available_width]
+        while format_width + wcswidth(msg) > available_width:
+            msg = msg[:-1]
+        msg += ellipsis
+
+    return format.format(msg)

@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from _pytest.terminal import _format_trimmed
+from _pytest.unicode_trimmed import unicode_trimmed
+import pytest
+
+
+def test_unicode_trimmed_fits() -> None:
+    msg = "unconditional skip"
+    assert unicode_trimmed(" ({}) ", msg, len(msg) + 4) == " (unconditional skip) "
+
+
+def test_unicode_trimmed_ellipsis() -> None:
+    msg = "unconditional skip"
+    assert unicode_trimmed(" ({}) ", msg, len(msg) + 3) == " (unconditional sk…) "
+    assert unicode_trimmed(" ({}) ", msg, 6) == " (u…) "
+    assert unicode_trimmed(" ({}) ", msg, 5) == " (…) "
+    assert unicode_trimmed(" ({}) ", msg, 4) is None
+
+
+def test_unicode_trimmed_first_line_only() -> None:
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "first\nsecond", 10) == "first"
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "first line\nsecond", 6) == "first…"
+
+
+def test_unicode_trimmed_wide_chars() -> None:
+    # Each CJK character has a display width of 2.
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e", 6) == "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e"
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e", 5) == "\u65e5\u672c…"
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e", 4) == "\u65e5…"
+
+
+def test_unicode_trimmed_empty() -> None:
+    assert unicode_trimmed("", "", 0) is None
+    assert unicode_trimmed("", "", 1) == ""
+    assert unicode_trimmed("{}", "", 1) == ""
+    assert unicode_trimmed("({})", "", 3) == "()"
+    assert unicode_trimmed("({})", "", 2) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("fmt", "msg", "width"),
+    [
+        (" ({}) ", "unconditional skip", 30),
+        (" ({}) ", "", 10),
+        ("{}", "abc", 3),
+        ("{} {}", "abc", 10),
+    ],
+)
+def test_unicode_trimmed_matches_format_trimmed_when_untrimmed(
+    fmt: str, msg: str, width: int
+) -> None:
+    try:
+        expected = _format_trimmed(fmt, msg, width)
+    except Exception as e:
+        with pytest.raises(type(e)):
+            unicode_trimmed(fmt, msg, width)
+    else:
+        assert unicode_trimmed(fmt, msg, width) == expected
notes:
Added unicode_trimmed mirroring _format_trimmed line-for-line, but with a single '…' whose display width (via wcswidth) is used for the fit check and trimming; terminal.py is unchanged. Added tests covering trimming, wide chars, multi-line, empty inputs and parity with _format_trimmed.
